title: Process for 26/11 trial in absentia of Lashkar handlers Saeed, Lakhvi starts
content: India has launched a trial in absentia for six accused linked to the 26/11 terror attacks. This initiative, guided by the new Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, aims to expedite justice. A special court has declared Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi as fugitives, utilizing evidence from Ajmal Kasab’s confession to connect them to the tragedy. Interpol is also stepping in to issue red corner notices for these suspects.

title: 'Which RSS, BJP man fought for nation?' Kharge hits back amid Vande Mataram row
content: During a spirited gathering led by Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress workers passionately sang Vande Mataram, igniting debates over the BJP's accusations of disrespect towards the national anthem. Kharge swiftly defended the party's honor, emphasizing the need for unity and solidarity amidst their internal disputes. He held the state government accountable and pledged to tackle pressing local issues head-on.

title: Why Google is making headlines in Berkshire's biggest quarter of stock-buying
content: In a remarkable shift, Berkshire Hathaway has expanded its investment in Alphabet, acquiring approximately 106 million shares, marking its most significant stock purchase quarter in years. Additionally, the conglomerate escalated its Delta Air Lines investment by 44 percent, with total stock spending exceeding $23 billion last quarter. This change ends a 14-quarter trend of being a net seller.

title: 'Sab talvaar chalayenge': Pant's hilarious Jadeja banter caught on stump mic

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her approach allows acquiring and erasing patient debt at steep discounts. This model has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar initiatives. While philanthropic efforts provide immediate relief, policy reform remains stalled. Lasting change may require systemic reforms addressing the root causes of medical debt.

title: Hawaii’s 1905 mosquitofish import now linked to native species decline
content: The introduction of mosquitofish in Hawaii has dramatically affected the ecosystem, leading to notable declines in native aquatic insects. These invasive fish fiercely prey on local species, disrupting food chains. The native damselflies, unprepared for such predation, are particularly vulnerable, seeing their populations plummet. Additionally, mosquitofish compete with endemic fish and crustaceans for limited food resources, complicating control efforts due to intricate waterways and their fast breeding habits.

title: California startup's $3 billion 'manta ray' jet promises 50% lower fuel use
content: JetZero is unveiling a cutting-edge 'manta ray' aircraft aimed at revolutionizing the future of commercial aviation. This groundbreaking design is expected to yield impressive fuel savings and significantly lower emissions. With a full-scale prototype scheduled to take flight by 2027, Japan Airlines is on board to provide operational insights, paving the way for expected commercial operations in the early 2030s.

title: US student wins award for geometry breakthrough: How it can change modern medicine
content: Connor Hill won first place at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search competition.  His research classified noble polyhedra, identifying two infinite families and 146 isolated examples.  Hill translated a geometric problem into a finite algebraic one for a complete classification.  This method of reducing complexity is vital for modern biology and drug discovery.  His work demonstrates how mathematical simplification aids understanding in complex scientific fields.

title: Gen Alpha, Gen Z students march in Lucknow over shortage of teachers, amenities

The residential school students worried about upcoming board exams due to few classes.  Police intervened after the protest disrupted traffic and moved towards Hazratganj.  Senior officials resolved the situation by listening to student grievances.

title: Brittany Mahomes turns heads at Ella Langley concert after Chiefs loss

title: Twisha Sharma death by suicide, no sign of assault or struggle: AIIMS

title: 'Not a single protester died': Rijiju defends police action at Jantar Mantar
content: parliamentary affairs minister defends police response to student protests . he says security forces managed large crowds without casualties or serious injuries . "not a single person died; not even one protester is in the hospital with a serious injury," he said .

title: 'Victory for Jharkhand': Mahto ends 16-day hunger strike after Soren govt accepts demands
content: devendra Nath Mahto ended his hunger strike in the presence of state ministers dipika pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari . the government announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and all examinations conducted by TDPL . he thanked chief minister Hemant Soren, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, ministers and others who supported the students' agitation .

title: 'I apologise on his behalf': Vijay after minister's Karunanidhi reference
content: state forest minister apologises on minister's behalf for reference to late DMK leader . he refers to former CM and patriarch late M Karunanidhi by name . the reference triggered protests from opposition DMk members .

title: 'Every voter had valid ID': Trump praises India polls, renews push for SAVE America Act
content: president Donald Trump praised the election system in a post on Truth Social . he called for the passage of the SAVE America Act, which seeks to require proof of citizenship and voter identification in US elections . the proposed legislation seeks thwart thursday's election .

title: PDP chief Mehbooba says she is ‘dimagi Naxal’; NC blames her for Article 370 abrogation
content: mehbooba cited her support for Article 370 of the Constitution that granted special status to Jammu & Kashmir . the post prompted a jibe from governing NC, which blamed BJP coalition govt for its abrogation .
